key_insight: A nonstandard FEM-BEM and mixed FEM framework can solve the London equation in all of R^3 and reveal when off-axis vortex paths outperform the major axis in elongated superconducting geometries.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables accurate whole-space magnetic-field simulation for superconductors without artificial truncation, supporting better prediction of vortex nucleation sites in design studies.
method: Reformulate the magnetic potential as a transmission problem and couple FEM with BEM for the interior/exterior domains.
Compute the Helmholtz-Hodge component B_0 using Kikuchi's mixed formulation with a weak divergence-free constraint.
Discretize B_0 with H(curl)-conforming finite elements and apply it to the isoflux problem.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports convergence tests for the discretization and a geometric study showing that, in elongated ellipsoids, off-axis competitors can achieve larger isoflux ratios than the major axis.
watch_item: The off-axis maximizers imply rotational degeneracy, so the isoflux optimization may be non-unique and sensitive to geometry and numerical resolution.
paper_title: Numerical approach to the London Equation of superconductivity
